agree.reason: The plain apology, the weekly email promise and the credit for weeks when weather cuts a box by more than a third answer this household's complaint that the farm went quiet, though nothing addresses the money they lost last year.

honest.reason: Every claim traces to the brief or the user's facts, and the email openly says it can't promise there will be no crop loss and that the greens are still exposed.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are passed on raw: 'many of you' undersells 29 of 41 survey respondents (71%), and the email never works out the credit per week (about $24.50 of a $540 share) or what last summer's half-boxes cost the reader.

right_comparison.reason: The email sets last year's handling against this year's policy clearly, but it never describes the reader's real alternative, which is not rejoining or buying elsewhere.

qualification.reason: The 'more than a third' threshold and the weekly Thursday email give the reader a number and a schedule to check, but the email doesn't say how a cut will be measured or when the credit will be applied.

objections.reason: It meets the main objections of silence and no credit directly and admits the risk to the greens, but it leaves out the likely sore point that last year's loss gets no make-good.

fit.reason: It is a short, warm email with a subject line, a body of about 195 words and a clear deadline and sign-up path, as the brief asked.
